function: Target recognition in an integrated communication and sensing system: an LSTM generates RIS phases per sensing measurement and a learned decisioner sets the sensing duration (p. 5-8).
system: Full-duplex BS with ULAs (Nt=Nr=2 typical), single-antenna UE, OFDM; passive reflecting RIS of 20x20 to 50x50 elements, b-bit phases; 3 GHz (p. 3, 9-10, 15).
method: LSTM network with classifier, RIS-phase generator and learned decisioner; physical channel model in the loop; supervised end-to-end (cross-entropy) with curriculum training; temperature trick for discrete phases (p. 5-9).
data_channel: Custom physical channel model (LoS, single- and two-bounce RIS/target paths, Appendix A); targets from MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, synthesized images; MNIST 60,000 train, 10,000 test (p. 9, 15).
test_conditions: Same settings for training and testing on held-out test images; noise-free training then tested at other noise powers, with classifier retrained for new noise (p. 9-11).
baselines: Random RIS phases [21] and no RIS (non-learned); LISP [25] (learned RIS phases); GAMP imaging then CNN [22]; GRU variant; threshold-based decisioner [29] (p. 10-14).
metrics: Correct prediction rate (recognition accuracy) eta, average number of measurements, spectral efficiency loss versus communication-optimal RIS, training time and inference time (p. 9-14).
complexity: Inference under 1 ms per instance on an Nvidia 3090 GPU; training about 210 minutes, classifier retraining under 2 minutes; no parameter or operation count (p. 11).
openness: Part of the source code and the synthesized dataset at https://github.com/kiwi1944/CRISense (p. 1, 9).
q1_support: p. 9: "the CSI measurements can be generated with the physical channel model"; a custom free-space LoS and bounce model (Appendix A, p. 15), with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 11: "the noise power used during both training and testing is the same"; Scenarios 2 and 3 only change the noise power (an SNR change, with classifier retraining); no new scenario, dataset, array size or band.
q3_support: p. 10: "The LISP [25] and random [21] configurations are used as comparable baselines"; p. 11: "significant performance improvements of our proposed NNs over both the LISP method and random configurations".
q4_support: p. 11: "RIS phase generation in less than 1 ms per instance when using an Nvidia 3090 GPU"; training takes about 210 minutes. No parameter or FLOP count is given.
q5_support: p. 1: "Part of the source code for this paper can be accessed at https://github.com/kiwi1944/CRISense"; the synthesized dataset is released at the same link (p. 9).
notes: Included, area 5, as a borderline case: the learned RIS phases and sensing durations serve target recognition in a system that also communicates (time-division protocol, SE loss analysed on p. 12-13), while the communication RIS phases come from a non-learned algorithm [40] (p. 4, 16). If the reviewer reads this as sensing alone, the function exclusion would apply. q2: Table III (p. 11) adapts the classifier to new noise power, counted here as an SNR change. Tables and figures read from page images.
